_note: Boxes are NORMALISED to the tile (0-1). READ THIS FIRST: t011 is the RIGHT-HAND EDGE tile of the summit band and it overlaps t010 by 77% -- t011 x = t010 x minus 0.2336. Everything left of x 0.766 in this file is the same paint as summit-t010.json and the object ids are deliberately kept identical so a merge can deduplicate by name. Only the strip right of x 0.766 (master x 6072-6586) is new. Like t010 this is MOSTLY ROCK: a great pale wall of 牛毛皴 hemp-fibre strokes filling the upper two thirds, with the foliage crammed along the bottom edge and one tree fringe on the ridge at the top. THE DECOYS, all of them confirmed by zooming rather than guessed: (1) THE CENTRE-RIGHT CLIFF SHOULDER, x 0.40-0.78, y 0.10-0.65 -- strings of 点苔 moss dabs laid along every contour fold. This is the biggest false-positive surface in the tile and reads as ranks of pines at thumbnail size. No wood anywhere in it. (2) THE TOP RIDGE SPLITS IN TWO and the split is the single most useful observation in this file. Left of about x 0.545 the fringe resolves at 4x into layered flat pine crowns sitting on visible pale trunks -- REAL trees, catalogued. Right of x 0.545, from there out to x 0.80, the same fringe degenerates into single tapered vertical brush strokes: one stroke is one entire far tree, roughly 0.012 of the tile wide, with no leaf mass separable from the stroke. Those are left inside the rock object on purpose. The two halves look identical shrunk down and are completely different problems. (3) THE LOWER RIGHT SLOPE, x 0.60-1.0, y 0.60-0.85, is bare stone with fine parallel downhill strokes and a scatter of dabs -- the fan mimics hanging needles and contains no leaf glyph. THE ONE NEW TREE OBJECT this tile adds that t010 could not see: a small grove clinging to the right cliff at x 0.855-0.98, y 0.45-0.58, where at 6x there is a dark vertical trunk, two pale ochre trunks beside it, dark spreading canopies above and a blue-green wash underneath. t010 cut it off. Also, t010 saw only the left sliver of the blue-green tree at the bottom right; here the whole thing is in frame including its ochre limb at x 0.73-0.855, y 0.88-0.93, which is what proves the mass is a tree and not a wash. The bare 蟹爪 claw branches above the big blue-green tree at x 0.245-0.33, y 0.60-0.67 are wood with no leaves on them and will be caught by any dark-ink canopy mask -- exclude them.

objects.name: pale rock wall, upper left
objects.note: large empty silk face with a few long wandering contours and light dotting along the ledges. Same paint as cliff-mass-centre in summit-t010.json. Clipped by the top and left edges

objects.name: dotted cliff shoulder, centre right
objects.note: DECOY (1). Dense 点苔 dabs strung along every contour fold of the cliff; at thumbnail size the strings read as ranks of distant pines. Checked at 3x and 5x: dabs and hemp-fibre only, no stem, no branch, no leaf glyph. Same object as cliff-shoulder-right in summit-t010.json. NEVER animate

objects.name: ridge crest carrying single-stroke far trees
objects.note: DECOY (2), the right half of the top fringe. Deliberately labelled rock although it does contain trees: each far tree here is ONE tapered vertical brush stroke about 0.012 of the tile wide, with no leaf mass separable from the stroke that draws the whole tree. Far under the size floor and unanimatable. The boundary with the real pines to its left is at about x 0.545 and is worth checking by eye if a mask straddles it

objects.name: row of pines along the top ridge
objects.note: SEARCH REGION, and the only real foliage in the top half of this tile. At 4x each form is a flat layered pine crown standing on a pale vertical trunk -- genuine wood, checked because the cliff beside it is full of look-alike dotting. Individual crowns are about 0.025-0.033 of the tile across, under the floor, so this row moves as ONE soft mass or not at all. Same object as ridge-pines-upper-right in summit-t010.json

objects.name: small grove clinging to the right cliff
objects.note: NEW IN THIS TILE -- t010 cut it off at its right edge. At 6x: one dark vertical trunk at x~0.918, two pale ochre trunks beside it at x 0.923-0.947, dark spreading canopies above them and a blue-green wash underneath. Unambiguous wood, on a cliff otherwise made entirely of moss dots. SEARCH REGION -- the cliff shows through the gaps

objects.name: bare claw branches above the blue-green canopy
objects.note: dark 蟹爪 crab-claw twigs rising out of the top of the big tree above the leaf line, against empty silk. They read as a thin dark spray and any dark-ink mask cut for the canopy will grab them. They are wood. Same object as in summit-t010.json

objects.name: crown of the great blue-green tree, centre left
objects.note: broad canopy of small blue-green leaf strokes spreading right from the ochre trunk. The best-evidenced tree in this tile: trunk and right-sweeping limb are both plainly visible inside the box and are wood, not leaves. Same object as blue-green-tree-crown in summit-t010.json

objects.name: lower leaf curtain of the blue-green tree
objects.note: the canopy hanging below the main limb. Bottom edge at y 0.795 is where the leaves stop and bare slope begins; below that is stone

objects.name: ochre trunk of the blue-green tree
objects.note: clear pale-ochre vertical stem from the fork down through the canopy to the slope. Narrow, but it is the wood that makes the two leaf boxes above a tree. RIGID

objects.name: limb sweeping right out of the blue-green tree
objects.note: long ochre bough running out right through the canopy, visible in every gap between leaf clusters. A hinge should pivot the leaves about this line, not displace it

objects.name: yellow-ochre autumn canopy, clipped by the left edge
objects.note: dense tangled leaf strokes under a bright yellow-ochre wash, cut by the left edge. Its mass interlocks with the red-orange and tan crowns below and right of it -- they are three trees of one grove and no tight boundary between them exists. Same object as in summit-t010.json

objects.name: red-orange autumn canopy, bottom left corner
objects.note: small scale-like leaf marks under a strong red-orange wash, the most saturated passage in the tile. Clipped by both the left and bottom edges. Same object as in summit-t010.json

objects.name: tan autumn canopy, right of the yellow one
objects.note: peach-tan wash over the same tangled leaf stroke as its neighbours; the third crown of the bottom-left grove. Same object as in summit-t010.json

objects.name: blue-green leaf mass along the bottom edge, left of centre
objects.note: rounded blue-green 夾葉 clusters filling the bottom edge below the autumn grove. Clipped by the bottom edge; its wood is out of frame below, so trust the leaf glyphs rather than hunting for a trunk inside this box. Same object as in summit-t010.json

objects.name: dark pine clump below the blue-green tree
objects.note: dense dark-ink clump on the slope with trunk strokes legible at its base. SEARCH REGION -- it stands on open rock and roughly a third of this box is stone. Same object as in summit-t010.json

objects.name: orange autumn canopy, bottom centre
objects.note: salmon-orange wash over tangled leaf strokes, clipped by the bottom edge and isolated on bare rock, so its silhouette is clean on three sides. Same object as autumn-tree-bottom-right in summit-t010.json

objects.name: blue-green tree at the bottom right
objects.note: rounded blue-green 夾葉 clusters with dark outlines. t010 saw only the left sliver of this and had to guess; here the whole crown is in frame and the ochre limb running through it settles the question. Clipped by the bottom edge

objects.name: ochre limb inside the bottom-right blue-green tree
objects.note: a warm ochre bough curving through the middle of the leaf mass above. This is the wood that proves blue-green-tree-bottom-right is a tree rather than a wash on stone -- the same evidence was NOT visible in t010, which is why that tile's entry carries a caveat. RIGID

objects.name: blue-green leaf mass clipped by the right edge
objects.note: a second blue-green cluster running off the right edge of the tile and the bottom edge together. This is the true right margin of the painting, so nothing continues past it horizontally; the tree's wood is below the band

objects.name: hemp-fibre rock slope, upper right
objects.note: long parallel strokes running diagonally down the face with sparse dotting. Clipped by the top and right edges; this is the outer margin of the scroll

objects.name: bare hemp-fibre slope, lower right
objects.note: DECOY (3). Fine parallel strokes fanning downhill across a wide empty slope with a few smeared dabs. No leaf glyph, no wood. It sits directly above the real bottom-right blue-green tree, so this is the pair a colour or texture mask is most likely to merge by mistake. Same object as rock-slope-lower-right in summit-t010.json

objects.name: rock ground between the pine clump and the orange canopy
objects.note: pale contoured stone the bottom-band trees stand on, clipped by the bottom edge

objects.name: open slope below the blue-green tree
objects.note: the bare stone gap between the great blue-green tree's leaf curtain above and the orange canopy below. Almost empty silk with a few contours -- listed so a mask pass does not bridge the two foliage masses across it
